correctness.rationale: The matrix-unit Lindblad definition is trace-preserving and completely positive, and its exact Bloch generator, fixed point and strict stationary determinant are checked. The explicit yz-block eigenvalues and projectors give all coefficients through fourth order in the joint scaling. Direct Pauli-block substitution yields the fourth-order Schur complement with eigenvalues (1±exp(-s))/2. Perturbation of the eigenvalue-dependent Schur complement transfers this limit to the two small eigenvalues, with the other two tending to 1/2. Qubit PPT equivalence and upper-closed semigroup EB times prove the coefficient 4 and o(1) offset. Zero drive has exact negative Choi PT eigenvalue -exp(-t)/2 for all finite times. Numerical samples independently reconstruct the 4x4 PT matrix but are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The full primary-text comparison distinguishes the exact weak-resonant-drive, long-time Choi eigenvalue scaling and its zero-offset sharpness from published undriven amplitude-damping indices, primitive-semigroup eventual entanglement breaking, and general entanglement-breaking characterizations. Neither the existence theorem nor undriven-channel formulas imply the stated coefficient, boundary profile, or additive o(1). value.rationale: The first time a channel destroys arbitrary entanglement is a natural operational quantum-memory lifetime. Weak resonant driving has a singular effect on this invariant, unlike qualitative stationary mixing, and the sharp coefficient, zero-order offset, and universal eigenvalue crossover resolve the boundary quantitatively. This is neither a mere textbook substitution nor a narrow parameter lookup: it identifies the exact singular scaling of a standard driven-dissipative qubit model and the spectral mechanism causing it.
